crises.evidence: Unscheduled Cleanroom Fab Power Grid Malfunction & 5-Day Nitrogen Pipeline Maintenance
crises.rootCauseSummary:
Operational Disruption Briefing for CRX-SUP-NSM-TW:
NanoSilicon Microelectronics (Taiwan) experienced an abrupt fabrication outage affecting automotive microcontroller MCU-9021. With Pacific Hub inventory at 3,000 units and daily consumption at 1,500 units/day, existing stock covers only 2.0 days of production, posing an immediate line-down threat to Assembly Line 1 within 48 hours.

The Autonomous Central Orchestrator evaluated multi-agent inputs and synthesized the Hybrid Optimal Plan:
1. Dispatch an immediate inter-warehouse stock transfer of 1,800 units from Midwest Logistics Center (Chicago) via dedicated road freight (36-hour transit, $4,200).
2. Issue an emergency purchase order to Apex Semiconductor (Singapore) for 3,000 units with priority air cargo booking via Singapore Airlines ($48,600 total procurement & freight).
3. Throttle Fremont Line 1 production to 75% for 48 hours to extend current buffer by 1.8 days, aligning perfectly with incoming shipments.

Financial Assessment & Recommendation:
Total recovery investment is $52,800. This expenditure averts $520,000 in contractual customer SLA delay penalties and factory idle costs, delivering a 9.85x return on resilience investment while protecting 100% of Tier 1 deliveries to AeroDrive and MedPulse. Immediate human manager authorization is recommended.
